title: Prospective, randomized, controlled study on the efficacy of P6 acupressure as a prevention against postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV)
summary:
Many people feel unwell after surgery—they experience nausea or vomiting. This affects about one in three people and is considered particularly unpleasant by many.

Medications are usually prescribed to prevent or treat these symptoms. However, these medications do not work equally well for everyone and can cause side effects (such as fatigue, circulatory problems, or confusion).

That’s why we’re looking for other options that are effective and have as few side effects as possible. One of these is a technique called acupressure. It involves stimulating a specific point above the wrist with light pressure - for example, using an acupressure band. It doesn’t hurt, and no needles are used. This method is already used, for example, to treat nausea during pregnancy, motion sickness, or nausea caused by chemotherapy. However, it has not yet been sufficiently studied whether it is also effective after surgery. 

We would therefore like to find out whether acupressure really helps relieve postoperative nausea. To do this, we are comparing four groups of patients:

One group of patients receives an acupressure wristband that is correctly applied.
A second group of patients receives an acupressure wristband that applies pressure to a different, ineffective point (sham acupressure).
A third group of patients receives the proven standard medication for nausea.
A fourth group of patients receives no additional treatment.

All participants will receive the same type of anesthesia - what’s known as TIVA (total intravenous anesthesia). This is a form of general anesthesia administered through a vein that is very well tolerated. If nausea or vomiting does occur, however, these symptoms will be treated immediately, regardless of which group you are in.

interventions.name: Intervention “P6 Acupressure”: In the operating room, a CE-marked “Sea-Band®” - an elastic wristband with a built-in plastic snap button for mechanical stimulation of the P6 acupressure point - is applied to both wrists. The band remains in place for 24 hours postoperatively and is then removed.

Active control “sham acupressure”: A CE-marked “Sea-Band®” is also used, but its snap button is placed on the dorsal side of the forearm at the level of the P6 acupressure point, so that no targeted acupressure stimulation can occur. Active comparison “Standard pharmacological prophylaxis”: 30 minutes before the scheduled end of anesthesia, patients receive a single intravenous dose of 4 mg of ondansetron.
Passive control “No intervention”: In this group, no specific antiemetic measures are taken - only TIVA is used as a strategy for PONV prophylaxis.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•    Written consent obtained following comprehensive oral and written consultation
•    ASA classification I, II or III
•    Planned elective ENT procedure involving septoplasty and/or concha reduction or sinus surgery
Exclusion criteria:
•    Acupressure that cannot be performed or standardized, e.g., due to:
forearm circumference < 14 cm or > 21 cm, skin changes in the area of the acupressure point (e.g., burns, scars, local inflammation), metal implants in the forearm area, or previous removal of the radial artery (e.g., as part of bypass surgery)
•    Emergency surgeries
•    Use of antiemetics (e.g., H2-receptor antagonists, steroids) or opioids within 24 hours before surgery
•    Previous use of acupressure to treat nausea
•    Acute gastrointestinal symptoms (e.g., gastrointestinal infections, reflux symptoms) within the last 7 days
•    Need for follow-up care due to perioperative complications, in particular: transfer to an intensive care unit, need for reoperation
•    ASA classification ≥ IV
•    Current pregnancy or breastfeeding
•    Lack of adequate means of communication (e.g., due to a language barrier, cognitive impairment, or severe psychiatric illness)
